A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same entropy-weighted knowledge-distillation research, despite substantial revisions to its name and method. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support comparison throughout. v1 ends with references; v2 also includes readable supplementary Sections A.1–A.3.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and object-detection experiments on CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and MS-COCO, together with ablations and teacher–student alignment analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original vision experiments and GPT2 instruction-following distillation results. Its appendix adds empirical analyses of student entropy, loss landscapes, and learned representations.

M1.justification: v1 weights each sample’s distillation loss using teacher entropy alone. v2 introduces a student-dependent interaction, yielding wEA = HT(1 + HS/log(C))/2, so weights respond to the student throughout training (Section 3.2). It also specifies sequence-level reweighting for LLM distillation. These change the procedure beyond renaming ER-KD to EA-KD.

E1.justification: CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet classification and MS-COCO detection remain. v2 adds instruction-following language-model distillation evaluated on Dolly, SInst, Vicuna, S-NI, and UnNI (Table 6), substantially extending the represented domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: KD, CTKD, DKD, MLD, ReviewKD, and FCFD already participate in v1’s CIFAR-100 comparison and remain in v2. v2 adds MLD+LS to the CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet comparisons. Its new LLM comparison evaluates reverse KLD, JSD, and a supervised fine-tuning baseline alongside KD, substantially expanding the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The entropy temperature changes from 4 throughout v1 to 3 generally and 2 for transformer teachers in v2. One CIFAR-100 teacher changes from WRN-40-2 to WRN-28-4; the Tiny-ImageNet transformer comparison replaces the ResNet18 student with ResNet8×4 and revises teacher configurations. The reported Tiny-ImageNet validation count changes from 50,000 to 5,000, without establishing whether this corrects documentation or changes data use. New evaluations introduce ROUGE-L, CH indices, and Area@1.6 measurements.

E4.justification: v2 adds entropy-versus-inverse-entropy controls, teacher/student weighting-component ablations, training-time KLD analyses, DKD beta sensitivity, and extensive t-SNE analyses. The teacher-entropy segment comparison is retained, while loss-landscape analysis expands to multiple epochs and DKD, with KD results in Appendix A.2. v1’s entropy-density comparison, class-wise improvement plot, and output-discrepancy heatmaps are removed. The temperature ablation also changes its tested values and model pairings.

E5.justification: Five-run averaging is retained for the main classification comparisons. MS-COCO moves from an explicit three-run caption in v1 to v2’s general five-run statement; v2 also specifies five seeds for LLM results and newly reports three runs for transformer experiments. That transformer caption conflicts with the general five-run statement. Neither version provides confidence intervals or significance tests for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: Many results are replaced or added. For CIFAR-100 ResNet32×4→ResNet8×4, ER-KD’s 75.25 becomes EA-KD’s 75.46, while the DKD baseline changes from 76.01 to 76.32. Tiny-ImageNet’s corresponding proposed-method top-1 result changes from 59.93 to 59.39. Method and setting revisions prevent interpreting these as controlled performance changes. New LLM results report average ROUGE-L of 18.34 for EA-KD versus 17.63 for KD and 17.82 for RKLD; RKLD remains higher on SInst, 10.73 versus 10.59.

T1.justification: v2 adds an analytical argument under temperature 1 and a uniformly initialized student: nearly one-hot teacher outputs produce KL divergence near log(C), whereas uniform teacher outputs produce approximately zero (Equations 5–7). It also defines the combined entropy weight, its bounds, and limiting cases. v1 contains loss and integration formulas but lacks these arguments. The additions provide a mathematical rationale under specific assumptions, without a general performance guarantee.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on correcting student overconfidence through teacher-entropy reweighting. v2 centers it on identifying valuable samples and combining teacher and student assessments to adapt throughout training. Its abstract, contributions, and conclusion also extend the claimed applicability from vision experiments to LLM distillation.

C2.justification: v2 develops new interpretations connecting high entropy to decision-boundary knowledge, student entropy to evolving learning needs, and stable entropy to a feedback mechanism. It explicitly identifies static teacher-only weights as insufficiently adaptive and explains EA-DKD through complementary sample-level and class-level prioritization. These substantially extend and revise v1’s explanation based on overconfidence and overlooked dark knowledge.

D1.justification: v1 provides PyTorch-like pseudocode, framework-specific integration formulas, explicit epochs, batch sizes, learning rates, schedules, image resizing, and detection iterations. Much of this disappears in v2, which instead cites training recipes and gives a generic integration formula. v2 discloses the MLD+LS distillation-weight adjustment from 9.0 to 4.0. Its abstract replaces a stated available code repository and link with a future-release promise, materially reducing the supplied reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts from focal loss, hard-example mining, and general sample reweighting toward entropy-specific KD research. v2 adds Cheng et al.’s knowledge-quantification work and Kwon et al.’s entropy-based AKD, explicitly contrasting single-teacher high-entropy prioritization with multi-teacher reliability weighting. It also adds logit-standardization and LLM-distillation literature while dropping several earlier reweighting and adaptive-distillation references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, and analysis narrative are extensively rewritten. Detailed integration subsections give way to sections explaining loss imbalance, entropy interactions, and limiting behavior; related work replaces its sample-reweighting subsection with entropy-focused positioning. The title, terminology, author block, and supplementary organization also change.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is substantially redrawn, and the retained teacher-entropy accuracy plot is combined with a new t-SNE panel. New boxplots, training curves, sensitivity plots, and appendix visualization grids replace or supplement earlier displays. Loss landscapes change from final-model 3D surfaces to epoch-wise contour grids. Benchmark tables are reorganized to pair baselines with EA variants, distinguish method types, and display additional summaries.

improvement.justification: The new direction and component controls (Tables 1 and 8), sensitivity analysis, and actual LLM comparisons strengthen the weighting rationale and evidence of applicability beyond v1. These gains are limited by the removal of pseudocode, explicit training settings, and the stated code link. Conflicting run counts and unexplained EA-KD scores of 75.46 versus 75.27 in Tables 2 and 8 also weaken clarity. The added controlled evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
